metadata.title: 1966 Case 13
metadata.original_presentation: A thirty-six-year-old fish cutter was admitted to the hospital because of ulcers on the right leg and right forearm.

required.content: What is the patient's medical history and presenting symptoms?
required.response: He had been well until ten months previously, when he scraped his right leg on fish crates and was admitted to another hospital for treatment of 'fish poisoning,' which responded to penicillin therapy except for the development of 'lumps' on the right leg. Four months later 'lumps' also appeared on the arms and left leg. The lesions began as blisters and subsequently ulcerated. He became hoarse, lost 14 pounds in weight and stopped work because of generalized weakness.

teaching_points.content: Chronic skin lesions that ulcerate and are associated with systemic symptoms such as weight loss and weakness may suggest an underlying systemic disease or infection.

required.response: On readmission to the hospital a diagnosis of erythema induratum was made. Because of a positive tuberculin skin test isoniazid (INH) and para-aminosalicylic acid (PAS) were administered.

teaching_points.content: Erythema induratum is often associated with tuberculosis, and treatment may include anti-tubercular therapy.

required.content: What is the patient's social and family history?
required.response: He habitually smoked 3 packages of cigarettes daily and had always drunk 'his share of beer.' A brother had had clubbing of the fingers from birth. A bleeding disorder was known to exist in the family. He had hunted often and had been bitten by various animals.

teaching_points.content: Social habits such as smoking and alcohol consumption can impact overall health and may contribute to disease processes.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Erythema Induratum (Nodular Vasculitis)
supporting_evidence: diagnosis of erythema induratum was made
refuting_evidence: lack of improvement with INH and PAS
spread of lesions to arms and left leg
additional_information_needed: chest X-ray to rule out active TB

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Sporotrichosis
key_features: history of handling fish and potential exposure to contaminated water
supporting_evidence: ulcers on right leg and forearm
refuting_evidence: initial response to penicillin
lack of mention of lymphatic spread
additional_information_needed: history of exposure to plant material or soil

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cutaneous Anthrax
refuting_evidence: initial response to penicillin
lack of eschar formation
additional_information_needed: history of exposure to livestock or animal hides

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
refuting_evidence: initial response to penicillin
lack of systemic disease association

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Venous Insufficiency with Ulceration
refuting_evidence: spread to arms and left leg
weight loss and hoarseness

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: Physical examination revealed a slightly indurated annular area, 7.5 cm. in diameter, with a 1-cm. crusted border on the right forearm and a 2.3-cm. annular crusted lesion on the left forearm. An annular erythematous macule, 8 cm. in diameter, with a distinct border was observed on the abdomen. Areas of linear and arciform scarring, several centimeters in diameter, were observed on the legs. An arciform, elevated, indurated, bluish-pink lesion was present on the right calf; below it there was a circular, ulcerated, 2.5-cm. lesion with a central firm, black crust from which purulent material exuded. On the soft palate a 1-cm. punched-out ulcer with a necrotic base was seen. The lungs were clear, and the heart was normal. The edge of the liver was palpable 1.5 cm. below the right costal margin. There was marked clubbing of the fingers, but without cyanosis. Neurologic examination was negative.

teaching_points.content: Clubbing of the fingers can be associated with chronic hypoxia, lung disease, or other systemic conditions.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Erythema Induratum (Nodular Vasculitis)
supporting_evidence: diagnosis of erythema induratum was previously made
nodular and ulcerative lesions on extremities
refuting_evidence: lack of improvement with anti-tubercular therapy
presence of lesions on the abdomen and soft palate
additional_information_needed: further tuberculosis testing (e.g., chest X-ray, sputum culture)

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Sporotrichosis
key_features: history of handling fish or plants
refuting_evidence: lack of specific mention of lymphangitic spread
systemic symptoms like weight loss and hoarseness
additional_information_needed: culture of purulent material from lesions

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cutaneous Anthrax
supporting_evidence: ulcerated lesion with black crust on right calf
refuting_evidence: multiple lesions on different body parts
systemic symptoms not typical for cutaneous anthrax

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
refuting_evidence: lack of associated systemic disease history
lesions began as blisters

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Secondary Syphilis
supporting_evidence: systemic symptoms like weight loss and hoarseness
refuting_evidence: lack of specific rash pattern typical of syphilis
no mention of sexual history

required.content: What were the laboratory and imaging findings?
required.response: The urine gave a + test for protein; the sediment contained rare red cells and 3 to 6 white cells per high-power field. The hematocrit was 43 per cent; the white-cell count was 6000, with 67 per cent neutrophils, 4 per cent band forms, 18 per cent lymphocytes and 11 per cent monocytes. The urea nitrogen was 11 mg., the glucose 111 mg., the bilirubin 0.5 mg., and the protein 5.1 gm. (the albumin 3.3 gm., and the globulin 1.8 gm.) per 100 ml. The sedimentation rate was 3 mm. in one hour. The alkaline phosphatase and the glutamic oxalacetic transaminase (SGOT) were normal. The sodium was 123 milliequiv., the potassium 4.2 milliequiv., the chloride 98 milliequiv., and the carbon dioxide 20 milliequiv. per liter. An L.E.-cell test was negative. The cephalin flocculation was ++++ at forty-eight hours. The cold-agglutinin titer was 1:1. Culture of the urine yielded no growth; cultures of the throat and of the ulcerated lesion on the right calf yielded abundant Staphylococcus aureus. A tuberculin skin test (second-strength PPD) was positive. An electrocardiogram showed low voltage. X-ray films of the chest were normal except for bilateral basal linear densities; no enlarged lymph nodes were demonstrated. A film of the abdomen was normal.

teaching_points.content: Positive cultures for Staphylococcus aureus in skin lesions suggest a bacterial infection that may require targeted antibiotic therapy.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Erythema Induratum (Nodular Vasculitis)
supporting_evidence: diagnosis of erythema induratum was previously made
nodular and ulcerative lesions on extremities
refuting_evidence: lack of response to anti-tubercular therapy
presence of systemic symptoms like weight loss and hoarseness

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cutaneous Tuberculosis
refuting_evidence: lack of response to anti-tubercular therapy
negative chest X-ray for active TB
additional_information_needed: biopsy and culture of skin lesions for Mycobacterium tuberculosis

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
refuting_evidence: presence of Staphylococcus aureus in cultures
positive tuberculin skin test

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Staphylococcal Skin Infection
supporting_evidence: cultures of ulcerated lesion yielded abundant Staphylococcus aureus
refuting_evidence: systemic symptoms not typical for localized staphylococcal infection
lack of response to previous antibiotic therapy

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Wegener's Granulomatosis (Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis)
refuting_evidence: negative L.E.-cell test
normal chest X-ray
additional_information_needed: biopsy of skin lesions and/or nasal mucosa

required.content: What treatments were administered during the hospital stay?
required.response: Aqueous penicillin, 2,400,000 units daily, was administered, but the fever did not respond, and there was little change in the symptoms. Vincristine, 0.015 mg. per kilogram of body weight, was given, and a course of radiotherapy to the neck, 200 r daily for five days, was begun. Solumedrol, 80 mg. daily, was administered intravenously.

teaching_points.content: Vincristine is a chemotherapeutic agent used in the treatment of certain types of cancer, including lymphoma.

final_diagnosis.name: Malignant lymphoma
supporting_evidence: Systemic symptoms not responding to antibiotics
